style.title: Graceful capitals. Light, flowing words.
style.description: Your selected reference sets the direction throughout the course: fine lowercase, open capital ovals, and carefully placed shades. Complete alphabet and word models are drawn from the cited historical plates.
traits: Fine hairlines connect small, consistent lowercase letters.
Large open ovals give the leading capitals room to breathe.
A few tapered shades create emphasis while most curves remain light.
Long finishing strokes balance the words and leave clear space.
style.learningNote: Build light, consistent letters before adding larger flourishes. Study the complete source words for natural joins and spacing; use the individual letters to learn each form.
style.aiBrief: Aim for the user-selected handwriting direction: fine connected lowercase with consistent small-letter height; broad, open capital ovals; smoothly tapered selective shades on leading capitals; long light return curves and balanced white space. Preserve readable source-based letter construction and a consistent main slant: 50 degrees for the ornamental source models, or 52 degrees for classical foundations. Develop this character using the user’s own initials and name. Offer a repeatable daily version and, where relevant, a slower display version. These are described style qualities; no reference photograph is attached automatically.

examples.title: P and H: open oval capitals
examples.focus: Compare the fine oval returns with the selective, tapered shades in the P and H. These capitals are isolated from the photograph’s heading.

examples.title: P and S: balanced capital flourishes
examples.focus: Trace the large oval envelopes with a light movement. The shaded capital strokes stay inside open, unshaded return curves.

examples.title: C and O: controlled oval movement
examples.focus: Follow the continuous oval movement through the C and O, keeping the shaded segment selective and the return stroke fine.

examples.title: Z and B: signature capitals and finish
examples.focus: Study the balance between the ornamental Z and B and the broad terminal flourish. Use the curve relationships when composing your own initials.
